purpose: Restricted recovery U-Boot/ATF boot loader for the nx30pro immortalwrt-112m system layout

source.commit_ref_note: The commit is pinned; the ref name is informational only and must never be used to select a build input.

version_selection.evidence: The pinned fork documents SP1 as the pairing for a 5.4 kernel system, which is the kernel of the firmware this boot loader is built for.
version_selection.evidence_source: README.md of commit e4cf4dc72d451dc7a86c9508390ad5a2e50743c4: 'If you are using the 5.4 kernel or encounter issues such as hwrng wrong, try using the SP1 version or enable _MT7986_TRNG_NS_ACCESS in the ATF configuration.'
version_selection.evidence_note: This is upstream documentation, not a boot log of this device. Real boot compatibility with the 5.4 firmware stays UNRESOLVED until a device test.

rejected.reason: The pinned fork steers 5.4 kernel systems to SP1; the 2025 ATF pairing carries the hwrng problem the README names.
SP2 is the newest ATF pairing and has no documented 5.4 kernel compatibility statement.

build_script_trees.note: build.sh maps VERSION to UBOOT_DIR/ATF_DIR: 2025 -> atf-20250711, SP1 -> atf-20240117-bacca82a8, SP2 -> atf-20260123; UBOOT_DIR is always uboot-mtk-20250711. The build script is the only input that decides which tree is compiled, so the lock may not name another tree even when the repository carries one.

atf-20240117-bacca82a8.note: The ATF and U-Boot trees are vendored directories of the upstream repository, not submodules. Their revision is therefore the repository commit.

rejected_sources.reason: Upstream of this fork, but it carries neither the DHCPD web failsafe nor a multi layout defconfig for this board, so it cannot offer the locked layout whitelist. The 2023 U-Boot tree it builds was the base of the rejected earlier candidate.

build_env_notes.MULTI_LAYOUT: MULTI_LAYOUT=1 makes build.sh use configs/mt7981_h3c_magic-nx30-pro_multi_layout_defconfig, which enables CONFIG_MEDIATEK_MULTI_MTD_LAYOUT and carries no CONFIG_MTDPARTS_DEFAULT: the partition table then comes from the /mtd-layout node of the board device tree.
build_env_notes.FIXED_MTDPARTS: build.sh appends CONFIG_MEDIATEK_UBI_FIXED_MTDPARTS=y and CONFIG_MTK_FIXED_MTD_MTDPARTS=y. Upstream refuses MULTI_LAYOUT=1 together with FIXED_MTDPARTS=0, so the locked combination is the only supported one.
build_env_notes.SILENT: SILENT=Y answers the interactive fallback prompts of build.sh so that a missing multi layout defconfig fails the build instead of silently downgrading to the single layout defconfig.
build_env_notes.VARIANT: VARIANT=default keeps the raw mtd layout of this board. The ubootmod, ubi and openwrt variants force FIXED_MTDPARTS=0 and therefore cannot carry the multi layout whitelist.

patches.purpose: Makes immortalwrt-112m the default layout of an empty environment and disables the dangerous recovery web features on this board.
notes: board/mediatek/Kconfig gains CONFIG_MTK_DEFAULT_MTD_LAYOUT, a string symbol that depends on MEDIATEK_MULTI_MTD_LAYOUT and defaults to 'default', so no other board changes behaviour.
board/mediatek/common/mtd_layout.c replaces the four hard coded 'default' fallback labels with that symbol; the stock fallback stays when the symbol is unset.

Both board defconfigs disable the Factory, Flash, NAND raw, Console, Env, SIMG, UBI and Telnet features. The multi layout defconfig also selects immortalwrt-112m as the default layout. The single layout defconfig is hardened as well because build.sh downgrades to it when the multi layout defconfig is missing.

The bootstrap web UI records the layout the device currently uses, warns that pdt_data, pdt_data_1, exp and plugin are reclaimed, and asks for a confirmation before an upload switches away from the stock layout.
No partition table is patched: the pinned device tree already carries both locked layouts, and verify-layout-source checks that against the source.

toolchain.capture: The build report records the compiler path, the compiler version, the SHA-256 of the compiler binary (compiler_sha256), the dpkg package version and the apt candidate version of gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu. Upstream ships no toolchain checksum, so this record is the only evidence of the toolchain that produced the images.
toolchain.note: The upstream build script uses the host cross toolchain found on PATH. A different compiler revision changes the produced bytes, so a rebuild is only comparable when the recorded toolchain matches. The workflow installs the package from the distribution repository, so the recorded identity is the input that a rebuild has to repeat.
toolchain.reproducibility_acceptance: UNRESOLVED for this source. The earlier hanwckf based candidate produced different hashes on two clean runner builds because of an embedded build timestamp; the same question has to be answered again for this fork, whose artifact names also embed an md5 of the image.

host_package_notes.npm: build.sh runs 'npm install' inside uboot-mtk-20250711/failsafe/embedded and minifies the web failsafe assets before it compiles U-Boot. Without npm the build stops in the environment check.
host_package_notes.gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu: build.sh selects TOOLCHAIN_AARCH64 for every SoC except mt7629 and requires ${TOOLCHAIN}gcc on PATH.

board.name: h3c_magic-nx30-pro
board.tree_note: defconfig, multi_layout_defconfig and dts are paths inside uboot-mtk-20250711; atf_defconfig is a path inside atf-20240117-bacca82a8.
board.dram_note: The ATF DRAM initialisation is a prebuilt MediaTek object. The concrete DDR type and density must be read from the device boot log of this fork, the value recorded for the earlier candidate is not carried over.
board.boot_media_note: The board device tree enables spi_nand on spi0 and carries a bl2_verify node with bl2_compatible = "spim-nand", so the BL2 image is verified against the SPI-NAND boot medium.

selector.source: The web failsafe lists the labels of the /mtd-layout node of the pinned device tree. The device patch makes immortalwrt-112m the label that is used when the environment selects none, and it adds a data loss confirmation before a switch away from the stock layout.
selector.free_form_mtdparts_note: The upstream selector only offers a 'custom' entry when the mtd_layout_custom environment variable exists. That variable can only be written by the environment manager, which this build disables, or over UART. The device patch is rejected when it re-enables either path.

The flash editor reads and writes arbitrary storage ranges, which is an unrecoverable bricking path

overclock.note: The pinned tree carries no MediaTek CPU or DDR overclock Kconfig symbol; the only matches for 'overclock' are unrelated Rockchip and Atmel clock drivers. verify-config still rejects any enabled symbol whose name contains OVERCLOCK or a CPU/DDR/DRAM frequency setting, so a future upstream addition cannot pass unnoticed.

evidence.gate: verify-config reads the .config that olddefconfig produced in the U-Boot tree, never the environment that was passed to build.sh
evidence.source: failsafe/Kconfig gates every dangerous page and failsafe/failsafe_core.c registers its handler only when the symbol is set, so disabling the symbol removes the route as well

layouts.source_note: The whitelist is the /mtd-layout node of the pinned device tree. verify-layout-source reads that file and refuses a source that carries another layout set, so no layout is ever synthesised here.
layouts.address_space_note: Every table is addressed through the NMBM logical device nmbm0. A table addressed on the physical spi-nand0 device is rejected: the offsets are not physical NAND offsets.

immortalwrt-112m.label: immortalwrt-112m
immortalwrt-112m.note: The layout the paired 112M firmware is built for. It is the default of this build.

default.label: default
default.note: The stock layout of the device. It stays selectable so that a stock firmware can still be booted, and it is the only layout whose OEM areas can be backed up before a switch.

layouts.switch_warning: Switching from the stock layout to immortalwrt-112m reclaims pdt_data, pdt_data_1, exp and plugin into the UBI area. A read-only backup of the whole flash has to exist before the switch; the switch is not reversible from the 112M layout alone.

partition_contract.trailing_logical_space_note: The 112M layout of the pinned device tree ends at 0x7580000 and defines no partition behind it. The stock layout of the same device tree ends at 0x7800000, which is 122880 KiB in total. The remaining 2.5 MiB is therefore derived from the two source tables and not measured: the NMBM driver reports the available size from the block count of the loaded mapping, so the real capacity of a device can be smaller. The required logical end 0x7580000 is fixed; the observed logical capacity has to be at least that large, which stays UNRESOLVED until the device is read.
partition_contract.address_space_note: All offsets are addresses inside the NMBM logical space that the boot loader and the system expose. They are not physical NAND addresses and must not be used as such.

compatibility.upstream_stock_source: uboot-mtk-20250711/arch/arm/dts/mt7981-h3c_magic-nx30-pro.dts, /mtd-layout/layout@0 (label default), identical to CONFIG_MTDPARTS_DEFAULT of the single layout defconfig

mismatches.impact: The stock layout would treat the 112 MiB UBI area as a 64 MiB partition and could not install the factory image of the 112M system.
The 112M layout does not define this partition. Its content is part of the OEM data area and is reclaimed by the larger UBI partition.
Same as pdt_data. The paired firmware has to read the WAN MAC without it.

minimal_device_patch.scope: device-local build input only; the upstream tree stays unmodified in the source lock
minimal_device_patch.rationale: The pinned device tree already carries both required layouts: label default with the stock table and label immortalwrt-112m with the 112 MiB UBI table. No partition table has to be patched in. The remaining device patch of this build selects immortalwrt-112m as the default layout and disables the dangerous web failsafe features.

compatibility.mtd_layout_note: Both layouts live in the same pinned device tree, so the boot loader and the stock system agree on bl2, u-boot-env, Factory and fip and differ only in the UBI area and the four OEM partitions behind it.

nmbm.evidence_source: uboot-mtk-20250711/board/mediatek/Kconfig: NMBM_MAX_RATIO defaults to 1 and NMBM_MAX_BLOCKS defaults to 256 under ENABLE_NAND_NMBM; the board defconfigs do not override either value.
nmbm.note: The bootloader side of the geometry is verified in the pinned tree. The system side belongs to the firmware source, which is not locked yet, so the comparison stays unresolved instead of being asserted.

web_failsafe.address_source: CONFIG_IPADDR="192.168.1.1" and CONFIG_NETMASK="255.255.255.0" in the board defconfigs, exposed as the default ipaddr environment variable
web_failsafe.entry: The boot menu item for the web failsafe runs the httpd; with CONFIG_MTK_WEB_FAILSAFE_AFTER_BOOT_FAILURE the httpd also starts automatically when mtkboardboot cannot boot a system.
web_failsafe.upload_handler_source: uboot-mtk-20250711/failsafe/modules/upgrade.c accepts the form fields gpt, fip, bl2, firmware, simg, factory and initramfs. The gpt, simg and factory uploads belong to features this build disables.
web_failsafe.write_behaviour: UNRESOLVED until the effective configuration and a device test confirm the read back verification of this fork.
web_failsafe.verification_note: CONFIG_MTK_UPGRADE_BL2_VERIFY is set in the board defconfigs and the device tree carries a bl2_verify node, so a BL2 upload is checked before it is written. CONFIG_MTK_UPGRADE_IMAGE_VERIFY is explicitly unset in the board defconfigs; CONFIG_MTK_UPGRADE_FIP_VERIFY exists in board/mediatek/Kconfig and is not set by the board defconfigs, so a FIP upload is only verified by reading it back after writing.

artifacts.note: build.sh names both images with the md5 of the image itself, so the names change with every rebuild. The lock therefore records the name pattern of the locked BOARD/VERSION/VARIANT/FIXED_MTDPARTS/MULTI_LAYOUT combination, and the build has to resolve the pattern against the real output directory. Neither file is a system image and neither is a recovery image on its own.

system_dependencies.topic: WAN MAC source of the selected system
system_dependencies.source: UNRESOLVED: the firmware source of the redesign is not locked yet
system_dependencies.detail: The earlier candidate read the WAN MAC with mtd_get_mac_ascii from the pdt_data_1 partition (key ethaddr), which the 112M layout does not define.
system_dependencies.impact: The paired firmware has to read the WAN MAC without pdt_data_1 and without writing to the Factory partition.

system_dependencies.topic: Wi-Fi MAC and calibration data of the selected system
system_dependencies.source: UNRESOLVED: the firmware source of the redesign is not locked yet
system_dependencies.detail: The earlier candidate wrote a derived MAC into the Factory partition on first boot when the first two bytes at offset 4 were 00-0c.
system_dependencies.impact: A first boot that modifies the factory data area has to be ruled out before the layout is used, and the Factory partition has to be backed up first.
